questions.question: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the ________ directions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cardinal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Harappan civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was noted for its advanced urban planning.
 
• Cities in the Harappan civilization were planned with streets oriented along the cardinal directions, i.e., North-South and East-West.
 
• This alignment facilitated efficient drainage systems and optimized the use of sunlight and wind.
 
• The layout of streets and buildings indicates a high level of knowledge in geometry and urban planning.
 
• Major cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa exhibit this meticulous planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardinal Directions**

 
 
• The four main points of a compass: North, South, East, and West.
 
• Used in navigation and mapping for orientation and to determine direction.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning in Harappan Civilization**
 
 
• Included well-organized streets and sophisticated drainage systems.
 
• Homes were built with uniformity, often with baked bricks.
 
• The cities also had granaries, warehouses, and public baths.
 
 
 
• **Drainage Systems**
 
 
• Harappan cities had advanced drainage systems, with covered drains running along the main streets.
 
• Each house was connected to the main drainage system.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Findings**
 
 
• Excavations at Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, and other sites have revealed evidence of planned urban layouts and infrastructure.
 
• Artifacts such as seals, pottery, and tools provide insights into the daily life and trade practices of the Harappan people.

questions.question: The Megalithic site ________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inamgaon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Inamgaon is an important archaeological site located on the banks of the river Ghod, which is a tributary of the Bhima River in Maharashtra, India.
 
• The site dates back to the Chalcolithic (Copper Age) period, approximately between 1600 BCE and 700 BCE.
 
• Excavations at Inamgaon have revealed evidence of early farming communities, including the cultivation of crops such as barley, wheat, and legumes.
 
• Artifacts found at the site include pottery, tools, and ornaments, providing insights into the daily life and culture of the people who lived there.

• **Megalithic Culture:** Refers to a prehistoric period characterized by the construction of large stone structures or monuments, such as dolmens and menhirs.
 
• **Chalcolithic Period:** Also known as the Copper Age, this period marks the transition between the Neolithic (Stone Age) and the Bronze Age, characterized by the use of copper tools.
 
• **Excavation Techniques:** Archaeological excavations at sites like Inamgaon involve systematic digging and recording of artifacts to understand past human activities and cultures.
 
• **Ghod River:** A significant river in Maharashtra, India, it is a tributary of the Bhima River, which is part of the larger Krishna River basin.
 
• **Bhima River:** One of the major rivers in southern India, it flows through the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka and is a tributary of the Krishna River.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the animal motifs found on the cylindrical seal of the Indus region?

__
 
• **The humped bull** is one of the animal motifs found on the **cylindrical seal of the Indus region**.
 
• The humped bull figurine had a molded head that was twisted to the side, and a mold was used to make the head. The body was made by hand, and the head was connected. As with the enormous hollow bull statues, the eyes were crafted with applique pupils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It was one of three early civilizations of the Near East and South Asia, together with ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia, and it was the most widespread of the three, with sites reaching from northeast Afghanistan to much of Pakistan and western and northwestern India.

questions.question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dholavira, one of the most prominent archaeological sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, extensively utilized **stone** as a primary building material.
 
• The city’s structures, including walls, reservoirs, and gateways, were constructed using locally available stone, especially **sandstone and limestone**.
 
• Unlike other Harappan sites that predominantly used bricks, Dholavira is unique for its reliance on stone due to its geographical location in the arid region of Gujarat.
 
• The use of stone ensured durability and adaptability to the harsh climate of the Rann of Kutch, where Dholavira is located.
 
• The site’s sophisticated water management system, including reservoirs and drains, was also carved from stone, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dholavira:**

 
 
• Dholavira is located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, and is one of the largest Harappan settlements in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique urban planning and water conservation systems.
 
 
 
• **Water Management System:**
 
 
• Dholavira is famous for its intricate water management system, including reservoirs, step wells, and drains.
 
• This system reflects the ingenuity of the Harappan civilization in adapting to a water-scarce environment.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Architecture:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization is known for its urban planning, including grid-patterned streets, drainage systems, and standardized building materials like bricks and stones.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• While baked and unbaked bricks were common in most Harappan sites, Dholavira stands out for its extensive use of stone due to the availability of local resources.
 
• Other materials used included wood and mud for specific purposes like roofing and insulation.
